written.myAnswer: No. In free fall near Earth, heavier and lighter objects have the same acceleration due to gravity, so the heavier object does not fall faster.

Apply the equations of motion using g for acceleration due to gravity. Choose a direction as positive; quantities in the opposite direction are negative. For a released body, u = 0. For upward motion with upward positive, g is negative, and at the highest point v = 0.
